title: Double Cross
tagline: Draw a line. Close a box. Learn when to give one away.
teaser: The pencil-and-paper classic, lit up: take turns drawing lines, close a box to claim it and move again. Simple, until you learn why the best players hand over boxes on purpose. The computer that shipped with NetBSD never figured that out. You will.

manPage.synopsis: dab — draw a line; close a box to claim it and draw again; learn when to give boxes away.
manPage.description: A reborn dab, Christos Zoulas’s dots and boxes from NetBSD, its manual by Thomas Klausner. Its computer took every box it could see and never learned the double cross; here a ladder of five opponents climbs from that greedy mind to a solver, a tutorial and forty endgame puzzles teach chains and control, and a Daily Board starts everyone from the same opening.

howToPlay: Take turns drawing a line between two dots; close the fourth side of a box to claim it and draw again.
Boxes link into chains: whoever has to open a long chain usually hands over the rest.
Take all but the last two of a chain and hand those back, the double cross, to keep control.
